issues.description: validate_conda substring match accepts any executable whose --version output contains 'mamba' or 'conda'
issues.detail: The check `any(tool in out.decode().lower() for tool in [...])` accepts any binary whose --version stdout happens to contain those substrings (e.g. an unrelated tool printing a path or message). A stricter invariant — that the output starts with or matches a known program name — would make the validator's correctness statable. Also stderr is discarded; some tools print --version there.

issues.description: filters='*.exe' restricts the file dialog to Windows-only executables on macOS/Linux
issues.detail: Conda, mamba, and micromamba on POSIX systems are extensionless binaries. A user on Linux/macOS opening the browse dialog will see no matching files. The filter should be platform-conditional or omitted, since validate_conda already enforces correctness via os.access(..., X_OK) and the --version probe.

issues.description: validate_conda runs an external subprocess on every keystroke during path editing
issues.detail: If validate_callback is invoked on textChanged (typical for these line-edits), each keystroke spawns conda/mamba --version, which can take hundreds of ms and block the UI. The validator's complexity is dominated by process startup, not the file checks. Debounce, or only validate on editingFinished / focus-out, to keep the cost asymptotically reasonable.

issues.description: run_program(...).communicate() return value is not guarded against None stdout or non-utf8 bytes
issues.detail: out.decode() assumes UTF-8 and a non-None bytes object. On Windows some shims emit CP1252; on failure paths stdout can be empty. The except Exception catches decode errors but silently treats them as invalid — fine, but a literate comment stating that intent would help the reader follow the invariant 'unrecognized output means not-conda.'

issues.description: Local variable `valid` is set but immediately followed by `return valid`, while exception paths return False directly — inconsistent control flow
issues.detail: The function mixes early `return False` with a trailing `return valid`. Restructuring as a single exit (or all early returns) makes the loop-free invariant — 'valid iff file exists, is executable, and --version names a known tool' — readable in one glance. Minor, but this is foundational utility code that other reviewers will read.

issues.description: No literate comment explains why the fallback to custom conda_path lives inside the kernelspec argv() method
issues.detail: The new fallback in kernelspec.py reads as nested gates without naming the invariant: 'conda_exe is the auto-detected executable, or the user-configured override iff custom_conda is enabled, or we raise.' A one-line comment stating that invariant would let a future reader verify the logic without tracing both branches.

review.summary: The change is small, well-scoped, and mostly correct: a config flag, a preferences widget, a validator, and a fallback in kernelspec argv(). The algorithmic content is minimal, so rigor concerns focus on the validator and its use. validate_conda's substring match is loose enough that I'd call it UNDER-AUDITED — the invariant 'this binary is conda/mamba/micromamba' is not actually established by a substring scan of --version output. The Windows-only *.exe filter is a portability bug. The validator is also expensive (subprocess) and should not run on every keystroke; this is ASYMPTOTICALLY-OK-PRACTICALLY-SLOW territory if wired to textChanged. NEEDS-LITERATE-COMMENT on the kernelspec fallback. No P0 blockers.
